bugs.title: --edit on the file-disjoint fast-path runs N concurrent editors on one shared .git/STAGECOACH_EDITMSG file, silently attaching the wrong message to a commit
bugs.description: The v3.2 file-disjoint fast-path (FR-M13/FR-M14, runLoopFastPath) launches ALL N message generations CONCURRENTLY via goroutines (decompose.go:739-750). Each goroutine calls generateMessage, which unconditionally ends by calling generate.EditMessage when cfg.Edit is set (message.go:211). EditMessage writes the candidate message to a SINGLE fixed path — filepath.Join(gitDir, "STAGECOACH_EDITMSG") (finalize.go:77, written at finalize.go:91) — and then opens an interactive editor on that same path (finalize.go:97). With N>1 disjoint concepts, N editors open simultaneously in one terminal AND all read/write the same STAGECOACH_EDITMSG file, so the writers race: concept B overwrites concept A's file content before A's editor reads it back. The net effect, verified in a reproduction test, is that a concept receives ANOTHER concept's commit message: with two disjoint concepts whose generated messages were "feat: add a file" and "feat: add b file", BOTH published commits ended up with subject "feat: add a file" (concept 2 silently got concept 1's message), and two editor PIDs were observed running concurrently on the shared file. This is a silent correctness violation — the commit message no longer describes the commit's diff — and it directly contradicts FR-E4 ("In decompose mode, --edit gates each commit's message before its (already serialized) publication") whose word 'serialized' is load-bearing. The fast-path's own concurrency-safety comment (decompose.go:737-738) only reasons about the .git/index ("never touches the live .git/index") and is silent on EditMessage's shared-file write and interactive editor, so the hazard was not analyzed. The tooled-stager path (runLoop) is unaffected: its 1-deep overlap generates at most one message (and thus one editor) at a time, so editing is implicitly serialized there. Trigger: `stagecoach --edit` on a dirty, un-staged tree whose planner partition is pairwise file-disjoint (the common case for cleanly separated changes) with >=2 concepts.
bugs.reproduction: 1. In a git repo, make 2+ disjoint untracked/modified files with nothing staged. 2. Run `stagecoach --edit` (or set stagecoach EDIT / [generation].edit) so cfg.Edit=true, with a disjoint partition (>=2 concepts, no shared file -> isFileDisjoint true -> runLoopFastPath). 3. Observe: multiple $EDITOR instances open at once on the same .git/STAGECOACH_EDITMSG, and the resulting commits carry cross-contaminated messages. Confirmed in a focused test (internal/decompose, since removed): two editor PIDs (2704099, 2704100) ran concurrently; both editors saw 'feat: add a file'; both commits published with subject 'feat: add a file' even though concept 2's generated message was 'feat: add b file'. Code path: decompose.go:739-750 (concurrent launch) -> message.go:211 (generate.EditMessage) -> finalize.go:77,91 (fixed STAGECOACH_EDITMSG path) + finalize.go:97 (interactive editor).
bugs.location: internal/decompose/decompose.go:739-750 (runLoopFastPath concurrent launch); root cause spans internal/decompose/message.go:211 and internal/generate/finalize.go:67-97 (EditMessage uses a single shared .git/STAGECOACH_EDITMSG path)

bugs.title: File-disjoint fast-path loses cross-concept duplicate-subject detection: a single run can publish two commits with the identical subject
bugs.description: On the file-disjoint fast-path, all N message generations run concurrently BEFORE any commit is published (runLoopFastPath launches all goroutines at decompose.go:739-750, then publishes in CAS order in the serial loop that follows). Each generateMessage fetches recent commit subjects ONCE via messageRecentSubjects (message.go:120) and runs the duplicate-rejection loop (message.go:189, generate.IsDuplicate) against that snapshot. Because publication is serialized AFTER all generation, every concurrent generateMessage sees the SAME pre-run HEAD history — no concept can observe a sibling concept's just-produced subject. Consequently two disjoint concepts whose message agent emits the same subject both pass the duplicate check and both publish, yielding duplicate subjects in git log from a single run. This violates US7 ('I want Stagecoach to guarantee no duplicate subjects, so that git log doesn't contain the same line twice') and the FR30-FR33 duplicate-rejection guarantee as experienced by the user. The tooled-stager path (runLoop) does NOT have this regression: it generates message[i] only AFTER publishing concept[i-1] (publish(inflight) precedes launch of the next message), so the fresh recent-subjects fetch includes concept[i-1] and cross-concept duplicates are caught. FR-M14 enumerates the invariants the fast-path preserves (tree-to-tree diff, CAS serialization, freeze) but is silent on dedupe, so the guarantee was dropped implicitly. Verified in a reproduction test: two disjoint concepts (a.txt, b.txt) with a fixed-output message stub both published subject 'chore: update thing'; the control on the shared-file path did not. Trigger realism: any decompose run where the model produces a coincidentally identical subject for two distinct concept diffs (e.g. two unrelated 'fix typo' / 'add config' changes) — uncommon but realistic, and exactly the case US7 exists to prevent.
bugs.reproduction: 1. Repo with one baseline commit. 2. Create two disjoint untracked files (a.txt, b.txt), nothing staged. 3. Planner returns count=2 single=false with concepts files=[a.txt] and files=[b.txt] (pairwise disjoint -> isFileDisjoint true -> runLoopFastPath). 4. Message agent returns the SAME subject for both concepts (e.g. a fixed 'chore: update thing', or any model output collision). 5. Result: two commits both with subject 'chore: update thing' in git log. Confirmed in a focused test (internal/decompose, since removed): result.Commits subjects = ['chore: update thing','chore: update thing']; git log showed the subject twice. Code path: decompose.go:739-750 (all messages launched before any publish) -> message.go:120 (messageRecentSubjects fetches pre-run history only) -> message.go:189 (IsDuplicate sees no sibling).
bugs.location: internal/decompose/decompose.go:739-750 (runLoopFastPath concurrent launch before serial publish); dedupe fetch at internal/decompose/message.go:120,318 and check at internal/decompose/message.go:189

summary: Hunted the v3.2 file-disjoint staging fast-path (G29, FR-M13/FR-M14) and the provider-docs sync end-to-end against the PRD. Method: read the full fast-path implementation (runLoopFastPath in internal/decompose/decompose.go, the git primitives it reuses, generateMessage, EditMessage, verifyFreezeSubset, the arbiter gate), confirmed git's `add -- <path>` stages deletions on git>=2.0 (so deletion-only and nested-dir disjoint concepts work correctly), probed renames (correctly split: claimed path in the concept, the unclaimed side flows to the arbiter), and wrote throwaway reproduction tests (since removed) to confirm two real concurrency bugs. Both stem from the same root cause: runLoopFastPath runs generateMessage concurrently for all concepts, but generateMessage contains two operations that are NOT concurrency-safe under that fan-out. (1) BUG-001 (critical): with --edit, N concurrent editors open on the single shared .git/STAGECOACH_EDITMSG file, racing so that a concept silently receives another concept's commit message (verified: both commits got concept 1's message). Contradicts FR-E4's 'serialized' editing. (2) BUG-002 (major): because all messages generate before any publish, cross-concept duplicate-subject detection is lost and one run can emit two identical subjects (verified), contradicting US7/FR32; runLoop does not have this regression. Note: I also initially observed a committed cursor.toml missing tooled_flags (a real TestProviderReferenceFiles_DecodeParity failure), but a concurrent process committed the fix (5980a44 'docs(provider/cursor): sync reference file + spec/doc with the cursor stager') during the hunt, so it is resolved in current HEAD and is NOT listed above. The full existing test suite passes (go test ./internal/decompose/... ok); both bugs require the specific scenarios above and are not covered by the current suite. The fast-path's deterministic staging sweep, FR-M1c freeze enforcement, FR-M8 empty-skip, FR-M7 CAS-ordered publish, FR-M12 isolation, and arbiter integration are otherwise sound.
recommendations: BUG-001: make --edit concurrency-safe on the fast-path. Either (a) defer EditMessage out of the concurrent generateMessage goroutine and perform it in the serial publish loop (one editor at a time, matching FR-E4's 'serialized publication' and mirroring runLoop's implicit serialization), giving each concept its own EDITMSG path; or (b) when cfg.Edit is true, fall back from the fast-path to the tooled-stager runLoop (which serializes editing via its 1-deep overlap). Option (a) preserves the concurrency win for the non-edit case.

BUG-002: close the cross-concept dedupe gap on the fast-path. Options include (a) after the concurrent generation sweep, run a serial dedupe pass over the N candidate subjects before publishing (retry/rescue any that collide with already-decided subjects in the same run), or (b) accept the trade-off explicitly by documenting it in FR-M14 and US7 (not recommended, since US7 is a headline guarantee).

Add regression tests: (1) --edit + disjoint fast-path asserts at most one editor runs at a time and each concept's edited message matches its own diff; (2) fast-path with a same-subject collision asserts no two published commits share a subject. The current suite uses per-concept distinct messages and never exercises these paths.
Tighten the runLoopFastPath concurrency-safety comment (decompose.go:737-738) so it accounts for EditMessage and dedupe, not only the .git/index, to prevent the same blind spot recurring.
